newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WIMBLEDON GRIND OUT 0-0 CUP DRAW AT LEICESTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WIMBLEDON GRIND OUT 0-0 CUP DRAW AT LEICESTER.

text.p: Wimbledon took a tentative step towards Wembley on Tuesday when they eked out a dour 0-0 draw at Leicester in the first leg of a League Cup semifinal.
The Londoners, the only side in England still realistically challenging on all three domestic fronts, will now be favourites to win the return tie at Selhurst Park.
That would take them into their first Cup final since 1988 when they beat Liverpool at Wembley to lift the F.A. Cup against all odds.

Leicester, who fought back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 against Chelsea in the F.A. Cup on Sunday, showed similar determination on Tuesday, especially in the second period when they pinned Wimbledon back into their own half.

Highly-rated forward Emile Heskey grazed a post in the final minutes and his striking partner Steve Claridge squandered a clear chance when he dragged a shot inches wide of Neil Sullivan's left-hand post.
But Wimbledon, conquerors of Manchester United in the F.A. Cup, kept their nerve and held on for a valuable draw.
Leicester's new signing Robert Ullathorne, in the side just hours after arriving from Spanish side Osasuna, was pulled off after 12 minutes when he caught his studs in the turf.
